APPENDIX C [Table 1, Item (iii)]
DETERMINATION OF SUBSIDIARY COLOURING MATTERS C-1 PROCEDURE C-1.1 Dissolve about 80 mg of sample in 100 ml chloroform. Apply 400 l of this solution as a streak 2 cm from the bottom of a TLC plate (Silica gel 0.25 mm). Immediately develop the chromatogram with a solvent mixture of 95 parts dichloromethane and 5 parts diethyl ether in a saturated chamber, suitably protected from light, until the solvent front has moved 15 cm above the initial 1

Amend No. 1 to IS 6405 : 1971 streak. Remove the plate, allow the main part of the solvent to evaporate at room temperature and mark the principal band as well as the bands corresponding to other carotenoids. Remove the silica gel adsorbent that contains the principal band, transfer it to a glass stoppered 100 ml centrifuge tube and add 40.0 ml chloroform (Solution 1). Remove the silica gel adsorbent that contains the combined bands corresponding to the other carotenoids, transfer it to a glass stoppered, 50 ml centrifuge tube and add 20.0 ml chloroform (Solution 2). Shake the centrifuge tubes by mechanical means for 10 min and centrifuge for 5 min. Dilute 10.0 ml of Solution 1 to 50.0 ml with chloroform (Solution 3). C-1.2 Determine, with a suitable spectrophotometer, the absorbances of Solutions 2 and 3 in 1 cm cells at the wavelength maximum about 485 nm, using chloroform as blank. C-2 CALCULATION C-2.1 Carotenoids other than canthaxanthine, percent = where A2 = absorbance of Solution 2, and A3 = absorbance of Solution 3. A2 � 100 10A3 + A2

DETERMINATION A-l. A-l.1 REAGENTS Chloroform shall be purified as follows: Wash the chloroform thrice with 10 percent aqueous solution of sodium thiosulphate in a separatory funnel. Dry the chloroform with

anhydrous calcium chloride and filter. Distil the chloroform over anhydrous sodium thiosulphate in all glass apparatus with a fractionating column of 70 cm length. Collect only middle fraction of the distillate, discarding the first 10 percent and last 10 percent. A-l.2 A-1.3 A-2. Cyclohexane Alcohol -pure. absolute.

PROCEDURE in Appendix A of IS: 6386-

A-2.1 Procedure shall be the same as given 197 1 * with the following exceptions.

A-2.1.1 The assay should be carried out rapidly, avoiding exposure to air and light. Weigh accurately about 90 mg into a loo-ml volumetric flask and dissolve in 20 ml of pure chloroform by Stirling. Check the solution by its transparency against a bright surface; if necessary, complete the dissolution by allowing to stand for a short while. Dilute to volume Pipette 5.0 ml of this solution into a loo-ml with pure cyclohexane. volumetric flask and dilute to volume with cyclohexane. Dilute 5.0 ml of this solution in the same manner to lOO*O ml. Measure the absorbance of this solution with a spectrophotometer at the maximum (approx 470 nm) in 1 cm quartz cells against cyclohexane as a blank. Calculate with E ( 1 percent, 1, cm ) = 2 200. A-2.1.2 Modijied Method for Water-Dispersible Materials-Weigh accurately about 120 mg of the substance into a stout walled test-tube. Add 10 ml of distilled water, flush thoroughly with nitrogen, and heat the test-tube in a water-bath at 60X, occasionally stirring with a glass rod. Care shall be taken that the powder is thoroughly wetted and that no particles reAfter approximately 10 main adhering to the glass wall of the test-tube. minutes complete emulsion of the powder should be obtained. Transfer the contents of the test-tube into a 250-ml volumetric flask and add 100 ml of absolute alcohol; use part of the alcohol also to rinse the glass rod and the test-tube. Add 100 ml of chloroform, rinsing the glass rod and test-tube again, shake vigorously, dilute to volume with chloroform, and Filter part of the solution and immediately pipette 5.0 ml of mix well. Flush with nitrogen and evathe clear filtrate into a round bottom flask. porate in a rotary evaporator at about 50�C to dryness. Moisten the residue with a few drops of absolute alcohol, add 50 ml of pure cyclohexane and completely dissolve by heating for a short time in a water-bath at 50�C. Transfer the solution quantitatively into a loo-ml volumetric flask, cool to room temperature and dilute to volume with cyclohexane. With a spectrophotometer, measure the extinction of the maximum at about 470 nm against cyclohexane at a blank, using l-cm cells. Complete the -___

APPENDIX [ yuble
DETERMINATION B-l. PROCEDURE

B

1, Item(ii) ]
OF SULPHATED ASH

B-l.1 Weigh accurately l-000 to 2.000 g of the material in a tared crucible. Ignite until thoroughly charred. Cool, then moisten the residue with one millilitre of sulphuric acid, and cautiously ignite until carbon is Conduct the ignition in a place protected from air completely consumed. currents, and use as low a temperature as possible to effect the combusion of the carbon. When the carbon has disappeared completely, cool the crucible in a desiccator and weigh. Note the weight as ash.
